entries.name: Alternating Cable Shoulder Press
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository as the vertical-press family base: standing tall with the cable running from the working hand to a low pulley; the hands press from shoulder height to straight overhead on the exact shoulder circle, and the turn between sides reads through the cable swapping hands (the far-limb resolver forbids per-frame one-arm asymmetry - the family-4 finding). Standard low-pulley setup chosen from the template; listed in the daily review. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Ten drawn positions of an alternating cable shoulder press, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Start with the near handle at shoulder height and the torso tall.
Press the near side up, stacking the wrist over the elbow.
Keep the ribcage quiet as the handle rises.
The handle nears the top of the press.
Finish overhead; then the far side takes its turn.
The far handle finishes overhead, ribs still quiet.
Lower the far side past the top of the press.
Keep the torso tall as the far side lowers.
Stay tall through the trunk on the way down.
Far handle back at shoulder height; ready for the next rep.

entries.name: Shoulder Press - With Bands
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: standing on the band with both hands at shoulder height, pressing both sides together overhead while the band stretches from the feet to the hands (longest at the finish). Standard under-foot band setup chosen from the template; listed in the daily review. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Ten drawn positions of a band shoulder press, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Start with the hands at shoulder height, standing on the band.
Press both sides together, staying tall.
Keep the ribcage quiet as the band stretches.
The hands near the top of the press.
Finish overhead; the band is at its longest.
Hold the top for a beat.
Lower both sides along the same path.
Stay tall through the trunk on the way down.
Ease back toward the shoulders.
Hands back at shoulder height; ready for the next rep.

entries.name: Standing Dumbbell Press
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: the arms started held forward at chest height and never finished straight overhead. Source-bound front-view draft: standing with the feet under the shoulders, the dumbbells at head height with the elbows out to the sides and the forearms upright; the dumbbells are pressed straight overhead until the arms are straight, a pause, and a slower lowering. The wrists stay over the elbows, and nothing below the arms moves.
entries.summary: Standing with the dumbbells at head height and the elbows out, press both overhead until the arms are straight without leg drive, pause, then lower under control.

frames.caption: Stand with the feet shoulder width apart and raise the dumbbells to head height, elbows out at about ninety degrees.
Brace, then press both dumbbells overhead until the arms finish straight, without leg drive or leaning back.
Pause. Finish overhead with a quiet ribcage.
Lower to the start under control.
Stay tall through the torso. Stack the wrists over the elbows.

entries.name: Standing Palm-In One-Arm Dumbbell Press
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: standing at an incline bench with one palm-in bell pressing overhead and the free hand braced steadily on the bench top; the bell is drawn standing vertical so the palm-in grip reads. Standard bench-braced setup chosen from the instructions; listed in the daily review. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Ten drawn positions of a standing palm-in one-arm dumbbell press, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Start with the bell at shoulder height, palm turned inward.
Press the bell up, palm turning inward.
Let the free hand steady you on the bench.
The arm nears straight overhead.
Finish fully extended, palm still inward.
Hold the top for a beat.
Lower until the elbow nears ninety degrees.
Keep the forearm stacked under the bell.
Ease back toward the shoulder.
Bell back at shoulder height; switch arms after the set.

entries.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics, pp. 388-389.
Saeterbakken, A. H., & Fimland, M. S. (2013). Effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses. JSCR, 27(7), 1824-1831.
entries.reason: Authored coordinate prototype with canonical 11-joint topology, seated back pad structure, and.

frames.caption: Sit against the pad with both dumbbells settled at shoulder height.
Press up while the upper back stays in contact with the pad.
Keep stacking the wrist over the elbow as the bells rise.
The bells rise along the same path, wrists stacked.
Finish tall overhead with both bells over the shoulders.
Lower along the same path, wrists stacked over elbows.
Control the descent back toward shoulder height.
The bells settle back to shoulder height.
Reset at shoulder height with the back still on the pad.

entries.summary: Nine drawn positions of a dumbbell shoulder press, seen from the side.

entries.name: Overhead Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 3 degrees, nearly side on: standing tall with balanced feet and a braced trunk, pressing the barbell close past the face, moving the head through to a tall lockout overhead, and lowering along the same path.
entries.summary: Standing with balanced feet and a braced trunk, set the bar across the front shoulders with a full grip and near-vertical forearms, press close past the face, move the head through to a tall stacked lockout, and lower along the same path.

frames.caption: Set the bar across the front shoulders with a full grip, forearms close to vertical, balanced feet, and a braced trunk before the bar leaves the shoulders.
Press close past the face without leaning the torso back into an incline press.
Move the head through to a tall, stacked lockout overhead with straight arms.
Lower the bar under control along the same vertical path past the face.
Return the bar to the front shoulders with the forearms close to vertical and the trunk braced.

entries.name: Arnold Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 32 degrees with a magnified hand close-up panel: standing tall and braced with dumbbells at shoulder height and palms facing in toward the athlete, pressing overhead while rotating the palms to face forward at lockout, and reversing the rotation on the way down without leaning back.
entries.summary: Standing tall and braced with dumbbells at shoulder height, elbows tight in front, and palms facing you, press overhead while rotating your palms to face forward at lockout, then reverse the rotation back to the start.

frames.caption: Stand tall and braced holding dumbbells at shoulder height with elbows tight in front and palms facing you.
Press up while smoothly rotating your palms outward and opening the elbows.
Finish at a tall, braced overhead lockout with the palms rotated 180 degrees to face forward.
Reverse the rotation smoothly on the way back down without leaning back.
Return the dumbbells to shoulder height with the elbows tight in front and palms facing you.

entries.name: Cable Shoulder Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 24 degrees with the low pulley set well forward of the feet and shins: standing tall with the handle at shoulder height, pressing one arm overhead to a stacked lockout against the low pulley's forward and downward pull, and lowering under control back to the shoulder.
entries.summary: Standing tall beside a low pulley set in front, bring the handle to shoulder height and press overhead to a tall stacked lockout against the cable's forward and downward pull, then lower under control back to the shoulder.

frames.caption: Set a low pulley in front and bring the handle to shoulder height, standing tall with the free hand at the hip.
Brace against the cable's forward and downward pull as you press the handle upward.
Press to a tall, stacked lockout overhead with the chest open and constant tension on the cable.
Lower the handle under control back toward the shoulder against the low pulley's pull.
Return to shoulder height with the trunk tall and braced.

entries.name: Alternating Kettlebell Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 34 degrees with a magnified hand close-up panel: standing tall with two kettlebells cleaned to the shoulders and palms facing in, pressing one kettlebell straight overhead while turning the palm forward as the other stays at the shoulder, lowering under control, and then pressing the other side.
entries.summary: Standing tall with two kettlebells cleaned to the shoulders and palms facing in, press one kettlebell straight overhead while turning the palm to face forward as the other waits at the shoulder, lower under control, then press the other side.

frames.caption: Clean two kettlebells to the shoulders with the palms facing in, and stand tall with the glutes squeezed.
Press one kettlebell straight overhead, turning the palm to face forward as it rises while the other bell waits at the shoulder.
Finish the first press with the arm straight beside the ear while the other kettlebell stays racked at the shoulder.
Lower the first kettlebell under control, turning the palm back in as it returns to the shoulder.
Press the other kettlebell straight overhead, turning its palm to face forward while the first bell waits at the shoulder.
Finish the second press with the arm straight beside the ear while the first kettlebell stays at the shoulder.
Lower the second kettlebell under control back to the shoulder to complete the alternating pair.

entries.name: Dumbbell One-Arm Shoulder Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 32 degrees with a magnified hand close-up panel: standing tall with one dumbbell at shoulder height and palm facing forward, pressing straight up to lockout, pausing at the top, and lowering slowly back to shoulder height.
entries.summary: Standing tall with one dumbbell at shoulder height, palm facing forward, and the other hand at your side, press the dumbbell straight up until the arm is straight, pause, and lower slowly to shoulder height.

frames.caption: Stand tall with ribs down, bring one dumbbell to shoulder height with the palm facing forward, and rest the other hand at your side.
Press the dumbbell straight up until the arm is straight overhead.
Pause at lockout with the trunk tall and ribs down.
Lower the dumbbell slowly toward shoulder height with the palm facing forward.
Return to shoulder height under control, complete the repetitions, then change arms.

entries.name: Kettlebell Arnold Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 34 degrees with a magnified hand close-up panel: standing tall with a kettlebell cleaned to the shoulder and palm facing in, pressing overhead while turning the wrist so the palm faces forward at the top, and lowering back to the shoulder while turning the palm back to face in.
entries.summary: Standing tall with a kettlebell cleaned to the shoulder and the palm facing in, press the kettlebell overhead while turning the wrist so the palm faces forward at lockout, then lower it back to the shoulder while turning the palm in.

frames.caption: Clean a kettlebell to the shoulder with the palm facing in, and stand tall with eyes forward.
Press the kettlebell up and overhead, turning the wrist as you press.
Finish at lockout with the arm straight and the palm turned to face forward.
Lower the kettlebell while turning the palm back in toward the shoulder.
Return the kettlebell to the shoulder rack with the palm facing in and the trunk tall.

entries.name: Kettlebell Seesaw Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 34 degrees: standing tall with two kettlebells cleaned to the shoulders, pressing one kettlebell overhead until the arm is straight, then pressing the other kettlebell up at the same time as the first lowers to the shoulder.
entries.summary: Standing tall with two kettlebells cleaned to the shoulders, press one kettlebell overhead until the arm is straight, then press the other kettlebell up as you lower the first to the shoulder in a continuous seesaw.

frames.caption: Clean two kettlebells to the shoulders and stand tall with the glutes squeezed.
Press one kettlebell overhead until the arm is straight.
As you lower the first kettlebell to the shoulder, press the other kettlebell up at the same time.
Finish the second press with a straight arm overhead as the first kettlebell reaches the shoulder, giving each side the same number of repetitions.
Lower the second kettlebell back to the shoulder rack while standing tall with the glutes squeezed.

entries.name: Double Kettlebell Push Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 28 degrees: dipping a few inches in a quick 330 ms knee bend while the torso stays vertical and the bells remain racked, driving the legs hard into full extension while the arms finish overhead at lockout over 820 ms, lowering back to the rack, and resetting between reps.
entries.summary: With two kettlebells in the rack, take a shallow, fast knee dip with a vertical torso, drive the legs hard to carry both bells to locked-out arms overhead, then lower back to the rack and reset.

frames.caption: Clean two kettlebells to the rack position with a vertical torso.
Dip a few inches by bending the knees with a vertical torso in a shallow, snappy dip.
Drive the legs hard and let that force carry both bells to locked-out arms overhead; the legs start the press and the arms finish it.
Catch the lockout overhead with both arms straight.
Lower back to the rack under control.
Rack, reset, and breathe between reps.

entries.name: Bent Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 32 degrees: keeping the kettlebell stacked over its base while the hips shift away and the torso wedges under it until the arm locks out, the head turned toward the bell (the head circle cannot show gaze), driving through the floor to stand tall under the locked arm, and lowering the bell straight to the shoulder rack.
entries.summary: With one kettlebell at the shoulder and the feet wider than the hips and turned slightly away, send the hips away and wedge the torso under the bell until the elbow locks while keeping the bell over its base, then drive through the floor to stand tall.

frames.caption: Clean one kettlebell to the shoulder, set the feet wider than the hips, and turn them slightly away from the loaded side.
Send the hips away and wedge the torso under the bell, straightening the arm as the body descends while the eyes stay on the handle.
Once the elbow is locked with the bell stacked over its base, drive the feet through the floor to stand tall.
Stand tall beneath a locked arm with the bell stacked over its base.
Lower the kettlebell back to the shoulder while standing tall.
Reset at the shoulder before the next repetition.

entries.name: Cuban Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 38 degrees: raising the elbows wide to shoulder height with the forearms hanging below them, holding the upper arms fixed while rotating the forearms up until the wrists stack over the elbows, pressing to a tall overhead finish with quiet hips, and reversing every stage under control.
entries.summary: Standing with very light dumbbells, raise the elbows wide to shoulder height with the forearms hanging, rotate the forearms around fixed upper arms until the wrists stack over the elbows, press overhead, and reverse every stage under control.

frames.caption: Stand tall with very light dumbbells at your sides.
Raise the elbows wide to shoulder height with the forearms hanging below them.
Keep the upper arms fixed while rotating the forearms until the wrists stack directly over the elbows.
Press to a tall overhead finish without the hips helping.
Hold the elbows high and wide and prepare to reverse the path smoothly.
Lower from overhead back to the stacked ninety-degree position with the wrists over the elbows.
Rotate around quiet upper arms until the forearms hang below the elbows again.
Lower the elbows from shoulder height back to the start under control.

entries.name: Eccentric Wall Handstand Push-Up
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 20 degrees: braced in one vertical line against the wall, lowering over a 4600 ms count (up to five seconds) until the head meets the pad softly, bringing the legs off the wall to land on the clear side without pressing out while inverted, resetting, and kicking back up for the next repetition.
entries.summary: With a firm padded target beneath the head and the hands just outside shoulder width against the wall, brace into a vertical line, lower for up to five seconds until the head meets the pad softly, exit to the floor on the rehearsed clear side, reset, and kick back up.

frames.caption: Clear the floor, place a firm padded target beneath the head, and kick to the wall with the hands just outside shoulder width in a vertical line.
Brace into a vertical line and lower for up to five seconds until the head meets the pad softly.
Bring the legs away from the wall toward the rehearsed clear side; the controlled lowering is the full rep.
Land the feet on the floor on the clear side.
Reset on the floor with the hands set outside shoulder width.
Kick back up toward the wall.
Find one strong vertical line against the wall for the next rep.

entries.name: Handstand Push-Up
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 20 degrees: kicking to the wall with the hands just outside shoulder width and a padded target beneath the head, bracing in one vertical line to lower until the head meets the pad softly, pressing back up to straight arms, and instructing the clear-side exit after the last repetition.
entries.summary: With a firm padded target beneath the head and the hands just outside shoulder width at the wall, brace in one vertical line, lower until the head meets the pad softly, and press back to straight arms.

frames.caption: Clear the floor, place a firm padded target beneath the head, and kick to the wall with the hands just outside shoulder width.
Brace into one vertical line and lower until the head meets the pad softly.
Meet the pad softly while holding one strong vertical line.
Press back to straight arms.
After the last repetition, exit through your rehearsed clear side.

entries.name: Pike Push-Up
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 22 degrees: holding the hips stacked high with the feet walked in and straight arms at the top, letting the elbows track back at about 45 degrees to lower the top of the head toward the floor just ahead of the hands, and pressing back to long arms without the hips drifting forward.
entries.summary: With your feet walked in and your hips lifted high in an inverted V, let your elbows track back at about 45 degrees from your body to lower the top of your head toward the floor just ahead of your hands, then press back to long arms without the hips drifting forward.

frames.caption: Start in a push-up position, then walk your feet in and lift your hips high so your torso points at the floor like an inverted V.
Let your elbows track back at about 45 degrees from your body and lower the top of your head towards a spot on the floor just ahead of your hands.
Keep the hips stacked high with the head just ahead of the hands.
Press back to long arms without the hips drifting forward.
Hold the high inverted-V hip stack at the top.
